terminal_record.title: Education Department Announces Reduction Affecting 1,315 Employees
terminal_record.description_short: On March 11, 2025, the Education Department announced a reduction affecting nearly half its workforce; ABC News reported notices to 1,315 employees.
terminal_record.description_medium: On March 11, 2025, the Department of Education announced a reduction in force affecting nearly half its workforce. The department’s release said its total workforce would fall from 4,133 at inauguration to roughly 2,183 after the action. ABC News reported that notices went to 1,315 employees; affected staff were set to enter administrative leave on March 21. The accessed sources do not establish direct DOGE direction.
terminal_record.description_long: The Department of Education announced a reduction in force on March 11, 2025. Its release said the action would affect nearly 50 percent of the department’s workforce and that impacted staff would be placed on administrative leave beginning March 21. The department listed 4,133 employees when President Trump took office and roughly 2,183 after the action; it said nearly 600 employees had already accepted voluntary resignation or retirement opportunities during the prior seven weeks. ABC News reported that reduction-in-force notices went to 1,315 employees on March 11 and that those affected were set to enter administrative leave on March 21, with pay and benefits through June 9. The department described the action as part of its “final mission.” This repaired account records the department’s announced workforce reduction and reported scale. The sources do not establish that DOGE directly ordered or carried out the reduction, so the frozen card’s DOGE attribution is omitted. The accessed sources also do not support the frozen card’s claims that particular program offices lost all staff, that compliance contacts disappeared, that complaints accumulated without staff, or that teachers unions called the action sabotage.

March 11, 2025

As part of the Department of Education’s final mission, the Department today initiated a reduction in force (RIF) impacting nearly 50% of the Department’s workforce. Impacted Department staff will be placed on administrative leave beginning Friday, March 21st.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: "Reduction in force" notifications went out to 1,315 employees Tuesday. Some 1,315 employees were affected by the RIFs, leaving 2,183 employed by the department, according to senior officials at the DOE. Impacted staff will be placed on administrative leave starting March 21, a statement from the Education Department said. They will receive full pay and benefits through June 9, senior officials added.
